title: tud, lehet, szabad: Putting the Three Together

sections.title: One question, three possible answers
sections.content: When someone asks Mit tudunk csinálni? ("What can we do?"), the honest answer often needs all three words together — what a person is able to do (tud), what the situation allows (lehet), and what the rules permit (szabad). None of these is "more correct" than the others; they simply answer different questions.

sections.title: tud vs. lehet vs. szabad
rows: Today it's possible to swim in the lake. (the situation)
Tudok úszni, és ma szabad is, úgyhogy lehet!
I can swim, and today it's allowed too, so it's possible!

items.spanish: Mit tudunk ma csinálni? Biciklizhetünk, vagy horgászhatunk a tónál.
items.english: What can we do today? We could cycle, or fish by the lake.

items.spanish: Van egy ötletem: menjünk piknikezni, ha szabad a parkban.
items.english: I have an idea: let's go have a picnic, if it's allowed in the park.

sections.content: A quick way to choose: ask whose limit you're describing. Yours personally → tud. The circumstances → lehet. A rule someone wrote down → szabad. When all three line up, the plan actually works.
